title: Cell Migration Assay Using Transwell Chambers
author: Marzia Ognibene
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgd9js96

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension
steps.instruction: Wash cells in cold PBS, detach with 5 mM EDTA, centrifuge at 1200 g for 7 min, and resuspend in serum‑free medium.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in serum‑free medium.

steps.title: Add medium to lower chamber
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL of complete medium to the lower chamber of each Corning Costar Transwell.

steps.title: Plate cells and incubate
steps.instruction: Place the desired number of cells in 100 µL serum‑free medium into the upper insert (8.0 µm pore size) of each Transwell and incubate at 37 °C for 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 100 µL serum‑free medium containing the cells into the upper insert.
Incubate the assembled Transwell at 37 °C for 24 hours.

steps.title: Add EDTA to adjacent well
steps.instruction: After the 24 h incubation, add 600 µL of 5 mM EDTA to an empty well positioned beside each used Transwell chamber.

steps.title: Transfer insert to EDTA well
steps.instruction: Remove DMEM from the upper insert and place the insert into the EDTA‑filled well.

steps.title: Collect lower chamber medium
steps.instruction: Collect the DMEM from the lower chamber and add EDTA to detach any cells that may have settled from the upper insert.

steps.title: Scrape migrated cells
steps.instruction: Using a plastic scraper, detach cells that have migrated to the underside of the upper insert and collect them in the EDTA well.

steps.title: Combine and centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Combine the cells collected from the lower chamber with those scraped from the insert in a single tube, centrifuge at 1200 g for 7 min, and then count the migrated cells.
